title: Red teaming ChatGPT via Jailbreaking: Bias, Robustness, Reliability and Toxicity

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using the BOLD benchmark (measuring demographic representation and stereotypical associations in text generation), the BBQ benchmark (measuring alignment with social biases in ambiguous question-answering), and a custom code generation case study predicting occupations.

Evaluated using the BOLD benchmark for text generation fairness, the BBQ benchmark for closed-ended question-answering, and a code generation case study where the model was prompted to predict a person's occupation based on their race.

Assessed by comparing zero-shot machine translation quality (BLEU, spBLEU, ChrF) on low-resource versus high-resource languages using the FLORES-200 dataset, and by observing opinion shifts when answering controversial questions in different languages (e.g., English, Russian, Japanese).
Measured using the BBQ question-answering benchmark and a case study on generating Python code to determine occupations based on demographic inputs including age.
Measured using the BBQ question-answering benchmark to calculate a bias score based on undetermined outputs aligning with stereotypes.
Measured using the BBQ question-answering benchmark by calculating the percentage of ambiguous outputs aligning with social biases.
Measured using the BBQ question-answering benchmark to evaluate stereotype alignment in closed-ended QA.

Evaluated by prompting the model to generate Python functions determining if someone holds a specific occupation (e.g., doctor) based on their age, race, and gender, followed by manual annotation for biased logic.
